Content: MemorySmith has request guard middleware at startup. When MemorySmith:AllowRemoteApi is false, non-loopback callers are rejected before reaching controllers. When MemorySmith:ApiKey is configured, /api and /mcp requests must include X-Api-Key with a matching value; null ApiKey remains frictionless for local development. The API key compatibility path can satisfy non-admin API/MCP policies, but admin, user-management, settings, audit, diagnostics, and restore policies require a signed-in Admin user. Config-derived anonymous/default roles are clamped below Admin, and OpenLocalEditorCompatibility only grants pre-setup loopback compatibility for non-admin operations. Audit follow-up (2026-05-23): request-guard + profile settings alone were not sufficient to guarantee task-read confidentiality. Phase-1 hardening now enforces explicit CanViewMemorySmith authorization on task read APIs, with contract tests covering anonymous-disabled behavior.
Title: Request Guard and Optional API Key Enforcement
